correctness.rationale: The set of points below the new point is a downset L, the set above an upset U; they must be disjoint and every member of L must be strictly below every member of U. These conditions also suffice by transitivity. Universality and homogeneity realize every such finite diagram over the fixed parameters and identify its realizations; arbitrarily many incomparable copies of the new point give nonalgebraicity. A fixed downset under σ is a union of cycles on the lower level, all of the lower level plus a nonempty union on the upper level, or all but one lower point together with its paired upper point at a fixed index. These contribute 2^c, 2^c−1 and f. Mixed diagrams are two nonempty disjoint unions of index cycles. There are 3^c−2^(c+1)+1 of these; after adding the one-sided diagrams and counting the empty pair once the result is 3^c+2^(c+1)+2f−2. Under στ a mixed diagram must swap its two index colors along each cycle; each odd cycle is therefore unused, each even cycle is unused or alternates in one of two phases. Including the empty diagram gives 3^e. As a separate orbit check, permutation averages of q^c and f are binomial(n+q−1,q−1) and 1; the average of 3^e is the coefficient of z^n in exp(sum_{k≥1} z^k/k + 2 sum_{k even} z^k/k)=1/[(1−z)(1−z²)], namely floor(n/2)+1. Burnside gives the two claimed orbit counts. At n=2 the counts are 19, 12 and 7, with no equality types included.
residual_risks: The twisted fixed count is for στ, not just for τ. Reversal acts on diagrams and is not an order-preserving automorphism of the ambient poset. The saved finite checks were inspected, not run, and are not an all-n proof.
